text:
liam: quick sync after the RFC follow-up meeting. high-level question: should we represent per-edge local leases as opaque blobs (signed by central) or as a small structured grant (tenant, quota_shard, count, seq, expiry)? i lean structured for easier reconciliation & partial audits.

nina: structured seems safer. opaque blobs are easy to forge mistakes with versions. structured + HMAC lets edges do cheap checks. plus we can include a tiny policy bitmask (e.g., `allow_burst`, `sample_traces`).

felix: tradeoffs: structured adds fields we might want to change later. versioning becomes important. propose lease v1 layout: `tenant_id`, `shard`, `tokens`, `expiry_ms`, `nonce`, `policy_flags`, `sig`. keep fields minimal so edge decoding is <32B.

tara: important to call out fairness scheduling needs: edges should not be free to preferentially drain one tenant's lease if central later detects abuse. central should track `outstanding_leases` per shard and apply decay when reconciling. also need a per-tenant global token cap so multiple edges can't collectively overshoot by abusing large shard counts.

liam: agreed. central stores two numbers per tenant: `committed_capacity` (what we guarantee) and `leased_outstanding` (sum of active tokens). edges reconcile reducing `leased_outstanding` on heartbeat. if `leased_outstanding` > `committed_capacity + tolerance`, central marks tenant for mitigation.

nina: define `tolerance` as a small multiple of median burst (e.g., 5%) plus an absolute floor (like 100 tokens) to avoid noisy mitigations for small tenants.

felix: on push vs pull: edges should pull for normal leases but central can push emergency revocations. push needs idempotency and integrity. push schema: `{ tenant, revoke_nonce, shrink_to, reason_code, ts }` with HMAC. edges apply shrink_to as a new local cap and start draining to that limit immediately.

tara: failure scenarios: network partition -> edges keep serving until lease expiry. necessary safety: leases should have conservative TTLs (30s default) and edges should degrade into deterministic local buckets after 3 missed heartbeats. deterministic means reject > committed_capacity.

liam: let's set conservative defaults: lease_ttl=30s, heartbeat_interval=10s, missed_heartbeat_threshold=3 -> degrade at ~30s.

nina: telemetry: we want `lease.issue`, `lease.consume`, `lease.reconcile`, `lease.revoke` events with small payloads. include `shard` and `nonce`. sample 0.1% of `consume` events with full trace for heavy tenants. add metric `lease.skew_ratio = leased_outstanding / committed_capacity`. alert when >1.15 for >2m.

felix: scheduling fairness: edges should implement a weighted round-robin across tenants using `committed_capacity` as weights. but local bursts can temporarily favor recent activity; central can smooth by reducing future lease sizes for tenants that frequently overshoot.

tara: abuse prevention: central ML scores (bot-likelihood, churn, ip-variance) should map to a `penalty_score` that reduces `committed_capacity` multiplicatively. score updates are applied at commit windows (1m) and pushed as lease-size hints. edges must not blindly honor hints older than 2 minutes.

liam: auditing: include `sig` on leases so that when a tenant disputes a rejection we can prove edge had a valid signed lease. keep HMAC key rotation: keys stamped `kid` in lease and rotate every 24h. store ks in central KMS and publish small jwk-like metadata to edges via control plane.

nina: proto sketch for events (compact): ```message LeaseEvent { string tenant = 1; string shard = 2; int64 nonce = 3; int32 delta = 4; int64 ts_ms = 5; enum Kind { ISSUE=0; CONSUME=1; RECONCILE=2; REVOKE=3 } Kind kind = 6; optional string trace_sample = 7; }``` we should make `trace_sample` conditional to keep payload small.

felix: also consider per-tenant hysteresis to avoid thrash: when central reduces capacity, apply a decay window (e.g., 2x window) before fully restoring. this prevents oscillation between edges and central.

tara: on the client surface: expose two error classes: `429.hard` (definite reject) and `429.soft` (local lease exhaustion) so app teams can implement backoff vs degrade behavior. document deprecation flow for apps that assume deterministic `429` semantics.

liam: infra-bot: can you create a TODO to add `lease.skew_ratio` alert and a dashboard card showing per-shard utilization?

infra-bot: Created ticket INFRA-7241: add lease skew alert and per-shard utilization panel. Runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/lease-skew. :white_check_mark:

nina: next steps: i'll write the follow-up RFC section on telemetry + alarms. felix will prototype lease encode/decode in the edge SDK. tara please draft the degraded-mode behavior for playbooks. liam will own the HMAC key rotation design.

liam: thanks all. aiming to publish RFC diff by Wednesday. tagging: @nina @felix @tara
